record.paper_title: Advances in periodic difference equations with open problems
record.original_question: Let f0, f1: S^1 → S^1 be continuous circle maps and consider the alternating system x_{n+1} = f_{n mod 2}(x_n). Characterize the set Per([f0, f1]) of least periods of periodic orbits for such 2-periodic systems on the circle, in the spirit of the interval result described by Theorem 2.1.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2.3. Extend Theorem 2.1 to periodic sequences of two continuous circle maps, that is, characterize the set of periods Per([f0, f1]), where f0, f1 : S1 → S1 are continuous.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S^1$ denote the unit circle. Given two continuous maps $f_0, f_1 : S^1 \to S^1$, consider the non-autonomous (2-periodic) discrete dynamical system
$$x_{n+1} = f_{n \bmod 2}(x_n), \qquad n = 0, 1, 2, \dots$$
A point $x_0 \in S^1$ is called periodic of least period $p \geq 1$ if $p$ is the smallest positive integer for which $x_p = x_0$ under the above iteration. Let
$$\mathrm{Per}([f_0, f_1]) = \{\, p \in \mathbb{N} : \text{the system has a periodic orbit of least period } p \,\}.$$
Provide a complete characterization of all subsets of $\mathbb{N}$ that arise as $\mathrm{Per}([f_0, f_1])$ as $(f_0, f_1)$ ranges over all pairs of continuous self-maps of $S^1$, in analogy with the known Sharkovsky-type characterization of $\mathrm{Per}([f_0, f_1])$ for continuous self-maps of a compact interval.
artifact.category_tag: periods of periodic orbits for non-autonomous circle maps
artifact.status_search_result: A literature search yields Sharkovsky-type results for autonomous continuous circle maps and extensions of Sharkovsky's theorem to periodic (non-autonomous) interval difference equations, but no published characterization of the period set Per([f0,f1]) for 2-periodic alternating systems of continuous circle maps was located. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: An extension of Sharkovsky's theorem to periodic difference equations
status_evidence.snippet: Extension of Sharkovsky's theorem and its converse to periodic difference equations on the interval.
status_evidence.claim: The interval analogue (the result the open problem aims to extend) is established for periodic difference equations on the interval.

status_evidence.title: Sharkovskii's theorem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Sharkovsky's theorem does not hold for continuous maps of the circle; e.g. rotation by 1/n yields only period-n orbits.
status_evidence.claim: The classical Sharkovsky theorem fails for autonomous continuous circle maps, indicating that an analogous characterization for the alternating case is non-trivial and not directly inherited.
